audits.title: Improving Allergy Status Documentation on Electronic Patient Records- a Trust-Wide In-Patient Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: NICE CG183: drug and reaction documented on all prescriptions and records; standard 100% of drug charts and Rio EPR with allergy status.
audits.setting: Older adult psychiatric inpatient units across Dudley, Walsall, West Bromwich and Wolverhampton, Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 100% of paper drug charts had allergy status but only 70% recorded type/severity; 62% had allergy status on EPR (30–100% by ward; Wolverhampton 93%, West Bromwich 100%, Dudley 33%, Walsall 39%).

audits.intervention: Allergy status prompt in electronic clerking document, stickers and posters on wards, pharmacy to update EPR allergy status, and allergy alert added to ward matrons' bed state view.
audits.other_findings: Re-audit across older and working age adult wards (about 300 patients) under way at time of writing.
audits.citation: Cook N, Prasanna A, Mathews R, Cabada J, Hebbar M, Jaffar S. Improving Allergy Status Documentation on Electronic Patient Records- a Trust-Wide In-Patient Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S83-S83.

audits.title: Assessing Recording of Allergy Status on Rio Amongst Patients in Sandwell CAMHS
audits.standard: NICE guidance on documentation of drug allergy status (substance, reaction, severity, date, evidence and certainty).
audits.setting: Sandwell CAMHS (Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust), Rio electronic record

cycle1.result: 60/516 had allergy status recorded (18 possible allergy, 42 no known allergy); 456 no recording. Of 18 allergies: reaction 12, severity 13, date 3, evidence/certainty 1.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations included Rio prompts for annual allergy updates, trust policy, junior doctor handbook/e-learning, and re-audit in 6–12 months.
audits.citation: Akhator-Eneka N, Maanuwa O. Assessing Recording of Allergy Status on Rio Amongst Patients in Sandwell CAMHS. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S168-S168.

audits.title: Audit of documentation of allergies in a psychiatric inpatient unit.
audits.standard: Gold standard guidelines on allergy documentation
audits.setting: Department of Psychiatry, Midland Regional Hospital, Portlaoise (acute and long-stay wards)

cycle1.result: Allergy section completed in 25% of medication charts; 12% of current case notes; 65% of original admission notes.

audits.intervention: Formal initial assessment proforma with a designated allergy section and promotion of awareness among NCHDs.

cycle2.result: Medication charts 58.1%; current case notes 19.1%; original admission notes 80.9%.

audits.other_findings: Current case notes improved only marginally.
audits.citation: Eneh O, Fahy S. Audit of documentation of allergies in a psychiatric inpatient unit. Ir J Psychol Med. 2011;28(4):213-216. doi:10.1017/s079096670001168x. PMID: 30200010.

audits.title: Quality of Drug Allergy Documentation in a Resource-Limited Paper-Based Hospital in Pakistan: Audit of Concordance and Completeness.
audits.standard: Five internationally recommended allergy documentation elements (drug, reaction, severity, date, treatment)

cycle1.result: Allergy status documented in 25.0% of clinical notes vs 94.3% of drug Kardex records (69.3 percentage-point gap).

audits.other_findings: Entries lacked actionable detail; structured five-element templates and allergy reconciliation workflows were suggested.

audits.title: Audit of ‘true’ penicillin allergies and their documentation in Milton Keynes University Hospital (MKUH)
audits.standard: ≥70% nature of allergy documented on eCare; ≥90% of eCare allergies also on Summary Care Record; 100% not given penicillin; ≥90% allergy label justified by nature of allergy
audits.setting: Milton Keynes University Hospital; inpatients with penicillin allergy

cycle1.result: Nature of allergy documented in 63.3% (n=57); also on SCR 85.6% (n=77); 93.3% (28/30) on antibiotics not given penicillin; justified allergy 50% (n=45). None of the four standards met.

audits.intervention: Planned: clinician training, new hospital guideline for a penicillin allergy de-labelling service, re-audit after 6 months.
audits.other_findings: Fewer patients than expected had a true penicillin allergy; patients could not be interviewed.
audits.citation: Kumar R, Ramm L. Audit of ‘true’ penicillin allergies and their documentation in Milton Keynes University Hospital (MKUH). International Journal of Pharmacy Practice. 2023;31(Supplement_2):ii29-ii29. doi:10.1093/ijpp/riad074.035.
